redFirst.basis: `python3 tools/check-committed-pii.py --selftest` in a throwaway tree at HEAD exited 1 with 1 of 45 collected tests failing an assertion, the task's own among them (named by --case, HEAD's own tests green on HEAD's code, the task's run with its inline suite tools/check-committed-pii.py laid over as HEAD's copy plus its 1 test hunk(s), 6 other hunk(s) held at HEAD), each passing with the working tree's implementation - q2i (house FAIL): SELFTEST FAILED: 44/45 cases passed; run without CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR; dependencies linked from the project root, entry by entry as symlinks: node_modules - .cache, .vite, .vite-temp are not linked and a new entry a runner makes beside the links stays in the throwaway, but a write into a linked entry lands in the project's own node_modules and is not watched; the user's .npmrc in the home directory dropped (every run has a fresh home)

outcome.technical: Unified the posix-home predicate the write scrub (_machine_paths.py) and the committed-artifact check (tools/check-committed-pii.py) each answered differently. Added _machine_paths.shape_fires (renamed from the module-private _shape_fires, now the one function both readers call) and a depth measurement (_segments_after/_TAIL_SEGMENTS/_HOME_PATH_MIN_DEPTH=3): a posix-home match fires when it carries a leading separator (as before), OR, with none, when the home word's own segment plus the further /segment pieces that continue it with no gap reach a depth of 3 - deep enough to be a home directory whose leading separator was cut (e.g. 'Users/<name>/p/x.js') rather than a sentence's words joined by slashes (e.g. 'home/cwd/project', 'home/TMPDIR', 'home/page.tsx', all depth <=2). tools/check-committed-pii.py now imports _machine_paths directly (plan gate refused editing plugins/audit/scripts/governance/_journal_io.py, which is outside this task's files and owned by other in_progress tasks, so the re-export tuple there was left untouched) and scan_text filters every DETECTORS match through _machine_paths.shape_fires(name, m) before appending it as a finding. Measured over this tree's committed artifacts by running the real scan (python3 tools/check-committed-pii.py): 17 posix-home BASELINE rows went dead (the P126 prose-recurrence rows plus the earlier 'home/TMPDIR' and 'home/page.tsx' rows the description points at) and were removed from BASELINE in the same change; the remaining posix-home rows (the CI runner's <outside-repo><r>/<r> example, the file-URL probe text) still carry a leading separator and stay found and baselined for their recorded reasons. A fresh run (`python3 tools/check-committed-pii.py`) now reports 'OK ... 34 finding(s); 34 accounted for by BASELINE' with no dead rows. Added test case q2i to tools/check-committed-pii.py's own selftest (tests.add's target) asserting both directions through the live DETECTORS pattern: a cut-separator home path ('Users/<user>/p/x.js') is found, a slash-joined prose phrase is not, and both outcomes come from _machine_paths.shape_fires. Also added mp16 to plugins/audit/tests/test__machine_paths.py pinning the same depth behaviour directly at the write-scrub's own door (in scope: the file is declared by this task). Ran: python3 plugins/audit/tests/test__machine_paths.py --selftest (19/19 pass), python3 tools/check-committed-pii.py --selftest (45/45 pass), ruff check (clean), vermin -t=3.8- (clean, min 3.3), and the full python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py (332/332 files ok, 15978 cases, exit 0). tools/prove-gates.py was read but not edited: shape_fires is not a *_violations/_drift/_claims-named function and does not walk the tree, so gate_names()/coverage() does not derive it and no TABLE row is owed.
outcome.descriptive: The PII check and the write scrub now agree on what a home path is, via one shared predicate, retiring 17 dead BASELINE rows the disagreement produced.
